arxiv-2111-05340.title: Symmetry conditions for the superconducting diode effect in chiral superconductors
arxiv-2111-05340.creator: Bastian Zinkl, Keita Hamamoto, Manfred Sigrist
arxiv-2111-05340.description: Abstract We analyze the presence of non-reciprocal critical currents, the so-called superconducting diode effect, in chiral superconductors within a generalized Ginzburg-Landau framework. After deriving its key symmetry conditions we illustrate the basic mechanism for two examples, the critical current in a thin film and a Josephson junction.

arxiv-2112-13384.title: Will You Dance To The Challenge? Predicting User Participation of TikTok Challenges PubID: pubid: Permission to make digital or hard copies of all or part of this work for personal or classroom use is granted without fee provided that copies are not made or distributed for profit or commercial advan
arxiv-2112-13384.creator: Lynnette Hui Xian Ng 1 , John Yeh Han Tan 2 , Darryl Jing Heng Tan 3 , Roy Ka-Wei Lee 3
arxiv-2112-13384.description: Abstract TikTok is a popular new social media, where users express themselves through short video clips. A common form of interaction on the platform is participating in “challenges”, which are songs and dances for users to iterate upon. Challenge contagion can be measured through replication reach, i.e., users uploading videos of their participation in the challenges.

arxiv-2205-07179.title: Promoting Saliency From Depth: Deep Unsupervised RGB-D Saliency Detection
arxiv-2205-07179.creator: Wei Ji, Jingjing Li, Qi Bi, Chuan Guo, Jie Liu, Li Cheng
arxiv-2205-07179.description: Abstract Growing interests in RGB-D salient object detection (RGB-D SOD) have been witnessed in recent years, owing partly to the popularity of depth sensors and the rapid progress of deep learning techniques. Unfortunately, existing RGB-D SOD methods typically demand large quantity of training images being thoroughly annotated at pixel-level.

arxiv-2206-00674.title: Refining the Cutoff 3d Gravity / T ​ T ¯ T\overline{T} Correspondence
arxiv-2206-00674.creator: Per Kraus, Ruben Monten, Konstantinos Roumpedakis
arxiv-2206-00674.description: Abstract Pure gravity in AdS 3 is a theory of boundary excitations, most simply expressed as a constrained free scalar with an improved stress tensor that is needed to match the Brown–Henneaux central charge. Excising a finite part of AdS gives rise to a static gauge Nambu–Goto action for the boundary graviton.

arxiv-2307-07396.title: Visualizing Overlapping Biclusterings and Boolean Matrix Factorizations
arxiv-2307-07396.creator: Thibault Marette, Pauli Miettinen, Stefan Neumann
arxiv-2307-07396.description: Abstract Finding (bi-)clusters in bipartite graphs is a popular data analysis approach. Analysts typically want to visualize the clusters, which is simple as long as the clusters are disjoint. However, many modern algorithms find overlapping clusters, making visualization more complicated.

arxiv-2308-10218.title: Reformulating the NMR Quantum Mechanics Fundamental Aspects: Spin 1 2 \tfrac{1}{2} Evolution in Magnetic Field Gradients
arxiv-2308-10218.description: Abstract Magnetization of a spin 1 2 \tfrac{1}{2} set is determined by means of their individual wave function. The theoretical treatment based on the fundamental axioms of quantum mechanics and solving explicitly Schrödinger equation gives the evolution of spin 1 2 \tfrac{1}{2} system driven by magnetic fields.

arxiv-2311-05117.title: Unsupervised Translation Quality Estimation Exploiting Synthetic Data and Pre-trained Multilingual Encoder
arxiv-2311-05117.creator: Yuto Kuroda, Atsushi Fujita, Tomoyuki Kajiwara, Takashi Ninomiya
arxiv-2311-05117.description: Abstract Translation quality estimation (TQE) is the task of predicting translation quality without reference translations. Due to the enormous cost of creating training data for TQE, only a few translation directions can benefit from supervised training. To address this issue, unsupervised TQE methods have been studied.

arxiv-2403-01502.title: Oscillating-charged Andreev Bound States and Their Appearance in UTe 2
arxiv-2403-01502.creator: Satoshi Ando, Shingo Kobayashi, Andreas P. Schnyder, Yasuhiro Asano, Satoshi Ikegaya
arxiv-2403-01502.description: Abstract Surface Andreev bound states, including Majorana bound states in topological superconductors, are typically charge neutral. In this work, we demonstrate the emergence of unconventional charged Andreev bound states in a superconductor with a sublattice degree of freedom, where the sign of charge density of the Andreev bound states oscillates between the two sublattices.

arxiv-2405-00235.title: Blockchain Price vs. Quantity Controls
arxiv-2405-00235.creator: Abdoulaye Ndiaye
arxiv-2405-00235.description: Abstract This paper studies the optimal transaction fee mechanisms for blockchains, focusing on the distinction between price-based ( 𝒫 \mathcal{P} ) and quantity-based ( 𝒬 \mathcal{Q} ) controls. By analyzing factors such as demand uncertainty, validator costs, cryptocurrency price fluctuations, price elasticity of demand, and levels of decentralization, we establish criteria that determine the selection of transaction fee mechanisms.

arxiv-2410-11187.title: Multiview Scene Graph
arxiv-2410-11187.creator: Juexiao ZhangGao ZhuSihang LiXinhao LiuHaorui SongXinran Tang, Chen Feng New York University
arxiv-2410-11187.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Juexiao ZhangGao ZhuSihang LiXinhao LiuHaorui SongXinran Tang, Chen Feng New York University. A proper scene representation is central to the pursuit of spatial intelligence where agents can robustly reconstruct and efficiently understand 3D scenes. A scene representation is either metric, such as landmark maps in 3D reconstruction, 3D bounding boxes in object detection, or voxel grids in occupancy prediction, or topological, such as pose graphs with loop closures in SLAM or visibility graphs in SfM.

arxiv-2504-10047.creator: A. Leviatan J.E. García-Ramos N. Gavrielov, P. Van Isacker
arxiv-2504-10047.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by A. Leviatan J.E. García-Ramos N. Gavrielov, P. Van Isacker. We show that a vibrational interpretation and good U(5) symmetry are maintained for the majority of low-lying normal states in 110,112,114,116 Cd isotopes, consistent with the empirical data. The observed deviations from this paradigm are properly treated by an interacting boson model Hamiltonian which breaks the U(5) symmetry in selected non-yrast states, while securing a weak mixing with coexisting SO(6)-like intruder states.
